item.title: Emergency services attending N4 crash
item.description: Gardaí and emergency services are currently at the scene of a crash in county Longford. The three-vehicle collision happened on the N4 in the Shroid area shortly before 3pm this afternoon. No injuries have been reported. Advertisement Motorists are being advised to avoid the area if possible.

item.title: No injuries reported following Leitrim crash
item.description: No injuries have been reported following a crash on the N4 in county Leitrim. Gardaí and emergency services attended the two-car collision which took place just outside of Drumsna shortly after 2.20pm. Significant delays continue to impact the road, however, it does remain open. Advertisement

item.title: Appeal issued over car suspected in Leitrim burglaries
item.description: An urgent public appeal has been issued following reports of a burglary gang in the Leitrim area. Gardaí are seeking to intercept a silver BMW 5 Series, 2008/2009 model, believed to be driven by a male driver and carrying up to four male occupants. The individuals are suspected are understood to be involved in a series of burglaries in the region. Advertisement Anyone with any information is being advised to contact Carrick-on-Shannon garda station on 071 965 0510.

item.title: Rain warning issued for Roscommon and Leitrim
item.description: A rain warning has been issued for Roscommon and Leitrim. The status yellow alert will run from 6pm on Saturday until midnight on Sunday. Met Eireann says there will be heavy spells of rain and a risk of flooding. Advertisement Poor visibility and difficult driving conditions are also expected. The rest of Connacht, and almost the entire western half of the country, will be under the same warning. Meteorologist Aoife Kealy has been looking ahead to the weekend: Advertisement

item.title: €38m in Food Waste Expected Across Shannonside Region in 2025
item.description: The Shannonside region is on track to throw away an estimated €38 million in food waste this year. Research from the Environmental Protection Agency indicates that the average Irish household wastes an estimated €700 of salvageable food annually. With the amount of occupied households in the region, this works out as €38 million in potentially wasted food over a 12-month period. item.title: Warning Issued as Rogue Couriers Target Midlands Residents
item.description: Authorities are issuing alert over rogue couriers in the Midlands. Vehicles purporting to be from DPD have reportedly been travelling the area in recent weeks. Gardaí have confirmed that the vehicles have no connection to the company. Advertisement Gardaí are urging anyone who sees the van, or who may have captured it or its occupants on a dash-cam or doorbell camera, to contact them immediately Authorities previously issued a warning about bogus callers in the Roscommon area.

item.title: More Than 400 Patients Face Treatment Delays Over 18 Months at Local Hospitals
item.description: Over 400 patients are waiting over 18 months for treatment at local hospitals. The most recent report from the National Treatment Purchase Fund reveals just over 8,400 inpatients were on the waiting list as of the end of November. A total of 4,884 are languishing on outpatient waiting lists at Sligo, Roscommon, Portiuncula and Mullingar hospitals. Advertisement As of the 27th of October, this number included 200 children.

item.title: St. Dominic's set for All-Ireland camogie final
item.description: Brídíní Oga won this title in January 2023 and the Glenravel outfit’s goal threat was the key in a six-point defeat of St Canice’s of Dungiven (Derry). item.title: Drumshanbo's Charlie McGettigan to return Eurovision trophy over Israel's involvement
item.description: Drumshanbo's Charlie McGettigan says he will hand back his Eurovision winners' trophy because of Israel's continued participation. Several countries, including Ireland, are boycotting next year's competition. They're furious Israel haven't been excluded because of their two-year war in Gaza.
